sections.title: 2 · 上周复盘
sections.body:
Quiet week that rewarded the one thing we actually committed to. The ledger settled nothing — zero commitments came due, and there were no prior reports in the archive to score against, so this is the first week with our own words on the page. That said, our one live idea earned its keep. We entered the el-nino-ag-2026 theme on 2026-09-06, and the DBA/MOS/NTR/DE basket led every sleeve we track over the week; nothing else on the board came close. The cross-asset backdrop was benign and confirmed the risk-on tone we'd have leaned into: rates.long eased, credit spread tightened another notch, and vol slipped back under the mid-teens — none of them arguing against the ag bid or against dispersion inside tech. Inside our sector map the story was cyclical-tech leadership with a software hole: sector:Memory/Storage and sector:Foundry ran hardest, sector:Computer/GPU followed, while sector:Cybersecurity and sector:Software/SaaS bled hard against SPY. That split matters because our nearest focus names, ADBE and ORCL, sit in the group that lagged — both report post-close 2026-09-10 and both carry rich IV ranks, so the week's software weakness is the tape walking into their prints, not away from them. We put no directional call on either, which was the right restraint given they hadn't printed. The one honest gap: fx and the DTWEXBGS row are stale to 2026-08-28, and commodities never answered, so any read on the dollar or crude behind the ag move is inference, not observation. Bottom line — a light week where our only real conviction, the ag theme, was also the week's best-performing basket, and our focus list correctly flagged the two catalysts that matter next.

sections.title: 4 · 下周展望
sections.body:
Item by item over what this week actually gave us.

The ag theme is the marquee item. It STRENGTHENS: the basket didn't just beat SPY over one week, it led on the four- and twelve-week windows too in the rotation table, and the kill switch is nowhere near armed. Wrong if the basket underperforms SPY over the coming week — the first weekly excess turning negative would be the tell that the move was a one-week squeeze, not a trend.

Memory/Storage and Foundry leadership CONTINUES near-term but is the most extended, so treat rank as fragile. Wrong if either sleeve flips to a negative weekly excess versus SPY next week while GPU holds — that would mark rotation out of the hardware complex.

The software/cyber weakness is the item to watch REVERSE, and the trigger is dated: ORCL and ADBE both print post-close 2026-09-10. A clean beat from either could pull the Software/SaaS and Cloud sleeves back toward the benchmark; a miss extends the hole. Wrong on the reversal call if both print and the sleeves stay red into the following week.

The macro tape CONTINUES risk-on: rates.long, credit and vol all moved the friendly way and none is at a level that forces a repricing before the 9/16 FOMC. That meeting is the hinge — the frame carries it as a live hike probability just above a coin-flip. For the risk-on read to REVERSE, the policy.path row would have to lurch toward a near-certain hike; a print that leaves it roughly where it sits keeps vol suppressed and the ag/hardware bid intact. Wrong if credit spread widens or vol pops back into the mid-teens ahead of the meeting.

The stale rows — fx and commodities — are the known blind spot. Until the DTWEXBGS series refreshes past 2026-08-28 and commodities answers, we can't confirm whether a softer dollar is underwriting the ag trade. Wrong to assume it is; watch for the fx row to actually update.
